summary: Second verification of the unreviewed 907-line P4 body of src/opt/api.py, reading each of the seven docstrings as a specification and then the body against it. The prior UNITS audit (.rework/audits/v_opt_units.json) covered clocks, the horizon and step indexing; nothing below repeats it. WHAT HOLDS. The param-group clause holds completely and I proved it the way the task asks: three base tensors handed to build() are all inside st.base, all three receive a gradient step (max|delta| 3.999e-05 each), an EMPTY group is constructed and counted rather than refused (torch does raise 'optimizer got an empty parameter list' for a bare [] and does NOT for [{'params': []}] -- the docstring's stated reason is true), a missing key becomes a counted empty group, and an unknown key is refused by name. All twelve declared startup refusals fire. The state_dict/load_state round trip is clean on EVERY field including the restart/damping state: after a run that damped once, restart_amp=0.5, cycle_best, cycle_index=8, lr_prev, shift_at=400 and all 1000 grad_norms come back, every DID IT FIRE counter round-trips except opt.ckpt.loaded which correctly increments, and lr_at at step 500 returns the identical rate before and after -- the 'came back at FULL AMPLITUDE' defect is dead. All four record types have every field the module docstring names, spelled as named, populated. Every name declared in a DID IT FIRE line IS produced by counters(). Every one of the 13 levers in src/opt/levers.py is read by at least one entry point. TEN DEFECTS SURVIVE, AND THE TWO WORST BOTH LAND ON GOAL A. (1) At OPT_LR_SCHED=none -- the module docstring's own 'one-flag ablation' for the hypothesis this package exists to test -- src/opt/api.py::_schedule returns the flat peak on its first line, yet counters() renders opt.lr.restarts, opt.lr.decay and opt.lr.shift_warm as 'armed, did not fire' with reachable=True, while the opt.lr.sched gate standing three lines above them says in its own reason that all of them are 'ALL structurally unreachable'. That is the exact collapse spine/gate.py exists to refuse, in the report the ablation will be read from. (2) src/opt/api.py::maybe_step's restart detector requires lr > 0.5 * opt.lr, and the package's OWN envelope and damping drive that false: on the 48,000-step / wavelength-6000 arm the docstring is about, 7 real restarts occur in the rate curve and opt.restart.detected reads 2; the closed loop that lr_restart_damp exists to run fires ONCE and is then permanently blind, because after two damps at the shipped damp=0.5 / min_frac=0.05 the restart peak is 0.2875 x lr, below the detector's own 0.5 x lr bar, forever. Also: a restart arriving with no Reading ERASES the inherited best (st.cycle_best = value unconditionally), so a 9.0 following a 2.0 is judged 'paid' and goes undamped; 'bit-identical to restarts=off at one fitted cycle' is false at every explicitly-set wavelength (899 of 1000 steps differ, up to 3.6x) and that false sentence is PRINTED by the opt.lr.restarts gate; counters() reads opt.lr_wavelength on the shipped-default path and does not declare it; build() declares lr_sched and never reads it; lr_at declares lr_restart_damp and never reads it. Suite green: ownership 12+18 / contract 14+46 / census 7 / assemble 9 / couplings 4, 0 failing; derive 575 oracle cases, 0 mismatches.

findings.detail: AT OPT_LR_SCHED=none FOUR GATES PRINT 'armed, did not fire' FOR MECHANISMS THAT CANNOT FIRE, AND THE GATE ABOVE THEM SAYS SO IN WRITING. src/opt/api.py::_schedule's first statement is `if sched == "none": return float(lr), (False, False, False, False)` -- warmup, the cosine, restarts, damping, the envelope and the shift re-warm are all downstream of that return and none of them is evaluated. But counters() builds opt.lr.restarts, opt.lr.decay and opt.lr.shift_warm from n_cycles, lr_decay, lr_shift_warm and opt.shift.notifications ONLY -- no branch of any of the three tests sched -- so each is emitted with the default reachable=True and renders through spine/gate.py::Gate.line as 'armed, did not fire'. spine/gate.py::Gate's own docstring defines that state as 'the mechanism ran and its condition was not met -- a measurement', and defines the other as 'the condition CANNOT be met on this configuration, which is not a measurement at all'. The contradiction is inside one report: the opt.lr.sched gate is constructed with reachable=True and the reason 'OPT_LR_SCHED=none: warmup, wavelength, floor, restarts, damping, envelope and re-warm are ALL structurally unreachable', so the report asserts unreachability in one line and then measures the same mechanisms as reachable in the next three. opt.lr.in_warmup additionally reads 0 as a bare integer with NO Gate at all in any configuration, so the ablation's warmup is the plain zero the three-state rule exists to forbid. THIS IS THE ARM THAT MATTERS: this package's module docstring names lr_sched="none" as 'the one-flag ablation' for the only hypothesis that explains all 17 pilots, and docs/04_CONTRACT.md line 1736 schedules the grad-clip measurement 'against the same seed set as the lr_sched="none" ablation'. The run whose DID IT FIRE surface is wrong is the run the project is about to take.

The rate is CONSTANT: the set of distinct StepOutcome.lr values over the whole run is exactly [0.002]. counters()['opt.report_lines'] then contains, in this order:

and ledger['opt.lr.in_warmup'] == 0 with no Gate keyed on it. Contrast the two gates in the same list that DO carry the third state: 'Gate opt.clip.applied: UNREACHABLE (0 vs n/a) -- OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 is OFF, so no step can clip. This is not "armed and did not fire".'

findings.detail: THE RESTART DETECTOR IS BLINDED BY THE TWO MECHANISMS IT FEEDS, SO THE ONLY CLOSED LOOP IN THE SCHEDULE RUNS AT MOST TWICE AND opt.restart.detected IS NOT THE RESTART COUNT. The body is `restart = bool(st.lr_prev > 0 and lr > 1.5 * st.lr_prev and lr > 0.5 * peak)`, matching the docstring character for character; the docstring justifies the SECOND condition solely as a warmup false-positive suppressor ('the warmup ramp climbs from zero ... each one was logged as a cosine restart (observed at steps 15 and 31 of an 18-epoch run, at 2% and 3% of peak)'). Nothing says it also discards genuine late restarts, and it does, because the restart PEAK is itself lowered by src/opt/api.py::_schedule's envelope (`cyc * ((1.0 - decay) + decay * env)`, shipped lr_decay=1.0) and by the damping (`cyc = min_frac + (cyc - min_frac) * restart_amp`). The damping half is algebraic and configuration-free: the peak of a damped cycle is lr * (min_frac + (1 - min_frac) * restart_amp), so at the shipped lr_min_frac=0.05 and lr_restart_damp=0.5 it is 0.525*lr after one damp (still detectable, barely) and 0.2875*lr after two -- permanently below the detector's own 0.5*lr bar. THE RATCHET SWITCHES ITS OWN SENSOR OFF AFTER AT MOST TWO APPLICATIONS, whatever the run length. Consequences on the DID IT FIRE surface: opt.restart.detected under-reports the run and is rendered by counters() against 'N cycles fitted', so a reader takes it as the restart count; opt.restart.readings under-reports for the same reason, and that counter's whole declared purpose is to make the UNREACHABLE verdict for the damping 'checkable instead of asserted'; and there is NO counter anywhere for a jump rejected by the second condition, so 'no restart occurred' and 'a restart occurred below the bar' are the same zero. This is the mechanism src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers.lr_restart_damp exists for -- 'the same losing bet re-taken three times at full amplitude', best 2.030 @ 252,000 -> final 2.848 -- and on the shipped defaults it gets to judge two of seven bets.
findings.repro: THE ARM THE MODULE DOCSTRING IS ABOUT: OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=6000 OPT_LR_WARMUP=1000 over 48,000 windows at the shipped lr_decay=1.0, lr_restart_damp=0.5, feeding a monotonically WORSENING Reading(value, seed_count=3) at every step so every restart is a losing bet. horizon = Horizon(run_steps=Steps(48000), warmup=Steps(1000), wavelength=Steps(6000), n_cycles=9). Upward jumps of >1.5x in the actual returned StepOutcome.lr occur at steps 6223, 11445, 16667, 21889, 27112, 32334, 37556 -- SEVEN real restarts. Only the first two clear 0.5*peak=0.001 (1.943e-3 and 1.778e-3; the third is 8.006e-4). Result: opt.restart.detected=2, opt.restart.damped=1, opt.restart.readings=2, restart_amp=0.5, and the report prints 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: FIRED (2 vs 9 cycles fitted)' and 'Gate opt.lr.restart_damp: FIRED (1 vs damp=0.5, refused_n1=0)'. Isolating the two causes over 1000 steps at wavelength=200 (8 real restarts): shipped -> detected 2, damped 1; OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0 (envelope off) -> detected 3, damped 2, restart_amp 0.25, then blind; OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0 with OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP=1.0 (both off) -> detected 8 of 8.

findings.detail: A RESTART THAT ARRIVES WITH NO Reading ERASES THE INHERITED BEST, WHICH LETS THE NEXT LOSING BET THROUGH UNDAMPED, AND RECORDS A REFUSAL THE REPORT SAYS CANNOT EXIST. The last line of the restart branch is `st.cycle_best = value` -- unconditional, and `value` is None whenever best_bpb is None. The docstring's clause 4 is 'if a restart fired and the cycle that just ended did not beat the best held-out IT INHERITED', and the field is named cycle_BEST; nothing licenses discarding the inherited value because this particular restart had no measurement. Two consequences. (a) THE NEXT RESTART IS UNJUDGEABLE: `paid = st.cycle_best is None or (...)` is True on a None best, so the following cycle is treated as having paid regardless of how bad its reading is, and is not damped. (b) THE REFUSAL COUNTER IS OVERLOADED: on the Reading-less restart itself, cycle_best is not None and value is, so `not paid` holds, and the seed count is 0, so opt.restart.damp_refused_n1 increments. That counter is documented in clause 4 as the PLAN 3.8 seed-count refusal -- 'OPT REFUSES TO DAMP on a seed count of 1' -- and counters()'s own gate text for the no-Reading state says 'with no Reading at all THERE IS NOTHING TO REFUSE'. Two different states, one number, and the state the gate says is empty is the one filling it. The repair cannot be read off the docstring (leave cycle_best alone, or refuse the restart outright), which is why this is reported and not proposed.
findings.repro:
OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=200 OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0 over 1000 steps, feeding Readings only at chosen restart steps: {200: Reading(2.0, 3), 300: None, 400: Reading(9.0, 3), 500: Reading(9.1, 3)}, None everywhere else. Observed, restart by restart:
  step 200 reading 2.0  -> cycle_best None -> 2.0,  amp 1.0, damped False   (correct: nothing inherited)
  step 300 reading None -> cycle_best 2.0  -> None, amp 1.0, damped False   (the inherited 2.0 is GONE; damp_refused_n1 += 1)
  step 400 reading 9.0  -> cycle_best None -> 9.0,  amp 1.0, damped False   (9.0 against an inherited 2.0 is the worst possible cycle and it is judged PAID)
  step 500 reading 9.1  -> cycle_best 9.0  -> 9.1,  amp 1.0 -> 0.5, damped True
Totals: readings=3, damped=1, damp_refused_n1=2, and the report prints 'Gate opt.lr.restart_damp: FIRED (1 vs damp=0.5, refused_n1=2)'.

findings.detail: 'AT EXACTLY ONE FITTED CYCLE THE SCHEDULE IS BIT-IDENTICAL TO lr_restarts=off' IS FALSE AT EVERY EXPLICITLY-SET WAVELENGTH, AND counters() PRINTS THAT FALSE SENTENCE INTO THE REPORT. The claim appears three times: in lr_at's docstring ('At exactly one fitted cycle the schedule is bit-identical to lr_restarts=off (:4785), which keeps every earlier result reproducible'), in _schedule's restarts-branch comment ('At n == 1 this branch is bit-identical to restarts=off'), and inside the opt.lr.restarts gate's UNREACHABLE reason, which is a printed report line. It is true only because the shipped lr_wavelength is the 0 sentinel. src/opt/api.py::_schedule prices the two branches against DIFFERENT lengths: restarts on uses `per_c = max(1.0, (run_end - w) / n)` -- the RUN -- while restarts off uses `span = max(1, wave - w)` -- the WAVELENGTH. They coincide only when wavelength == run_steps, which the sentinel forces. The same root revives both defects the restart machinery was introduced to kill, now reachable with OPT_LR_RESTARTS=off and a bare wavelength: a wavelength SHORTER than the run parks the tail at the floor (the docstring's own 'a 30-epoch run with 2 cycles and a THIRD of its length parked at the floor'), and a wavelength LONGER than the run ends it un-annealed (the E8 p=0.760 under-anneal the once-resolved horizon exists to prevent). The latter also falsifies lr_at's stated property 'the schedule's minimum over a whole run equals lr * lr_min_frac at EVERY restart count' post-warmup, which is a case the previous audit's restart-count sweep could not reach.
findings.repro:
run_windows=Windows(1000) at the defaults, pricing lr_at over steps 1..1000 with OPT_LR_RESTARTS on and off and diffing:
  OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0    n_cycles=1 -> 0 of 1000 steps differ (IDENTICAL -- the sentinel, and the only case tested before)
  OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=1000 n_cycles=1 -> 0 of 1000 differ
  OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=900  n_cycles=1 -> 899 of 1000 differ, e.g. step 550: 1.050e-3 vs 8.647e-4
  OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=800  n_cycles=1 -> 899 of 1000 differ, e.g. step 550: 1.050e-3 vs 6.378e-4, max ratio 3.600
  OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=1500 n_cycles=1 -> 900 of 1000 differ
and in all five cases counters() prints 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- ... so the schedule is bit-identical to restarts=off and no restart can occur.' Then with OPT_LR_RESTARTS=off over 1000 steps: wavelength=500 -> 502 of 1000 steps sit EXACTLY at the floor 1e-4; wavelength=1500 -> final rate 6.378e-4 against a floor of 1e-4, post-warmup minimum 6.378e-4; wavelength=0 -> final 1e-4, correct.

findings.detail: A LEVER READ THAT THE LEVERS READ LINE OMITS, ON THE SHIPPED-DEFAULT PATH -- the coupling family (47 survey records), direction two. counters()'s line is 'LEVERS READ: accum, batch_windows, lr_sched, lr_restarts, lr_decay, lr_shift_warm, weight_decay, lr_restart_damp, grad_clip'. The body also evaluates `int(opt.lr_wavelength)` twice, in the opt.lr.restarts gate's `elif n_cycles <= 1` branch: once to choose the reason ('the 0 sentinel makes one wavelength span the whole run' vs 'the period does not divide the run twice') and once to print OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH= into the reason string. That branch is not exotic -- it is what the SHIPPED configuration takes, because lr_wavelength=0 makes one wavelength span the run and n_cycles resolves to exactly 1. So every default run of this package reads a lever its own contract says it does not. tests/test_contract.py cannot see it and says so in its header: 'nothing about whether the levers a stub CLAIMS to read are the ones it will read ... A lever named in a docstring and never read by the body is invisible to this file'; K4 passes because build() and lr_at name lr_wavelength, so the lever is not orphaned tree-wide.
findings.repro: AST sweep of src/opt/api.py for `opt.<field>` where field is one of the 13 OPTLevers fields, bucketed per function, diffed against each function's parsed LEVERS READ/WIRES READ block: counters -> READ-NOT-DECLARED ['lr_wavelength'] at lines 1047 and 1050. Then build at the shipped defaults over Windows(1000) and read the report: 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- OPT_LR_RESTARTS is on and exactly ONE cycle fits: OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0 against a horizon of 1000 steps (the 0 sentinel makes one wavelength span the whole run), so the schedule is bit-identical to restarts=off and no restart can occur.' -- the lever's value is in the printed line.

findings.detail: THE NOT-DUE PATH RETURNS 0.0 AS 'THE RATE THE OPTIMIZER IS CURRENTLY AT', WHICH IS THE ONE THING ITS OWN COMMENT SAYS NOT TO DO. The branch is `return StepOutcome(stepped=False, lr=float(st.lr_prev), restart=False, damped=False)` under the comment 'THE RATE THE OPTIMIZER IS CURRENTLY AT, not a fresh one: no step was taken, so nothing rewrote the param groups, and returning a newly computed rate would tell FAB.own_lr_scale a number the optimizer is not using.' build() constructs both AdamW instances with lr=opt.lr and initialises st.lr_prev=0.0, and st.lr_prev is only written after a step. So on every not-due call before the first optimizer step the function returns 0.0 while the param groups genuinely hold opt.lr -- the exact failure the comment names, with the sign that looks safe. The value leaves the package: docs/04_CONTRACT.md's C1 ruling makes StepOutcome.lr the `applied_lr` argument of src/fabric/api.py::own_lr_scale, 'the LIVE rate ... for the lr_maxr ratio clamp', and spine/compose.py's LOOP_ORDER B row hands it over under exactly that spelling. Invisible at the shipped accum=1, where every call is due; at fetch_big.py's recommended heavy-run ACCUM=4 it is the first three calls of the run, and after any resume that restores lr_prev the value is at least stale rather than zero. An unconditional read of st.base.param_groups[0]['lr'] would answer the question the comment asks and needs no new state; I am reporting rather than proposing, since the return is a frozen record.
findings.repro:
OPT_ACCUM=4, one base tensor and one encoder tensor, scaled_backward + maybe_step per window. st.base.param_groups[0]['lr'] immediately after build() is 0.002. Then:

  backward 2: stepped=False, returned lr=0.0    , actual group lr=0.002
  backward 3: stepped=False, returned lr=0.0    , actual group lr=0.002
  backward 4: stepped=True , returned lr=0.00016, actual group lr=0.00016
  backward 5: stepped=False, returned lr=0.00016, actual group lr=0.00016   (correct from here on)

findings.detail: build DECLARES lr_sched UNDER LEVERS READ AND NEVER READS IT -- the armed-but-inert family (57 survey records), direction one, inside the declaration rather than in a launcher. build's line is 'LEVERS READ: lr, weight_decay, lr_warmup, lr_wavelength, lr_restarts, lr_restart_damp, lr_decay, lr_min_frac, lr_sched, accum, batch_windows, grad_clip'. `opt.lr_sched` appears nowhere in build's body: the horizon is resolved, the wavelength sentinel taken, the warmup clamped and n_cycles fitted identically whether the schedule is cosine or none, and every one of build's counters (opt.build.wavelength, warmup_clamped, cycles_fitted) describes a schedule that OPT_LR_SCHED=none guarantees will never be evaluated. That is not itself wrong -- the horizon is cheap and the report prints it -- but the LEVERS READ line is the tree's only machine-adjacent record of who reads what, tests/test_contract.py's header states plainly that it checks presence and not truth, and this entry is false. It also compounds the sched=none gate defect reported above: build resolves and PRINTS a nine-cycle horizon for a run whose rate is flat, with nothing in build's own surface marking it unreachable.

findings.detail: lr_at DECLARES lr_restart_damp UNDER LEVERS READ AND NEVER READS IT, AND ITS OWN BODY TEXT THREE PARAGRAPHS ABOVE SAYS SO. The line is 'LEVERS READ: lr, lr_sched, lr_min_frac, lr_restarts, lr_restart_damp, lr_decay, lr_shift_warm, lr_warmup, lr_wavelength (the last two through st.horizon)'. lr_warmup and lr_wavelength carry an honest qualifier; lr_restart_damp does not, and lr_at reads `float(st.restart_amp)` instead -- the accumulated product, which src/opt/api.py::maybe_step maintains. The docstring's own modifier bullet already names the right thing: 'restart damping, `st.cycle_index > 0 and st.restart_amp < 1.0`'. So one docstring states the dependency correctly in prose and incorrectly in the line that is parsed. The distinction is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: st.restart_amp travels in state_dict and lr_restart_damp does not, which is precisely the 'came back at FULL AMPLITUDE' separation state_dict's docstring is about, and a reader who trusts the LEVERS READ line concludes the schedule re-reads the lever each step.

findings.detail: TWO COUNTERS ARE PRODUCED THAT NO DID IT FIRE LINE AND NO DOCSTRING ANYWHERE DECLARES. The diff in the other direction is clean -- every name declared by any of the seven entry points is present in counters()' ledger -- but the ledger carries two entries whose only mention in the tree is the code that writes them. (a) opt.ckpt.horizon_changed: load_state increments it on exactly the resume state its docstring singles out ('REPORTS rather than refuses when the horizon changed'), yet its DID IT FIRE line reads only 'opt.ckpt.loaded, opt.ckpt.refused', and counters() gives it no Gate and no report line, so the one counter that says a resume changed the schedule's horizon is an unannounced integer in a dict. (b) opt.build.group_overlap: written by build from `len({id(t) for t in ordered[0][1]} & {id(t) for t in ordered[1][1]})` and printed in the opt.params report line, but named in no docstring in src/, in docs/04_CONTRACT.md, or in spine/compose.py -- so a nonzero value (a tensor in BOTH the base and encoder groups, i.e. one parameter stepped by OPT and again by SIG) is a number the report prints with no stated meaning. Related and softer: opt.build.params.base and opt.build.params.encoder ARE argued for in build's prose as 'the two numbers that make that visible' for the goal-B group-dropping hazard, but are absent from build's DID IT FIRE enumeration.
findings.repro: Parse the DID IT FIRE block of every public entry point in src/opt/api.py for `opt.*` tokens, then drive a run that exercises build, scaled_backward, maybe_step, state_dict, load_state and counters and diff against the returned ledger. DECLARED-but-absent: []. IN-LEDGER-but-undeclared, after discounting everything counters()'s own prose argues for (the accum invariant, the five named gates, the clip and grad-norm gates, the horizon triple, accum/batch_windows/d_effective_batch_windows, grad_norm.samples, restart_amp): opt.ckpt.horizon_changed and opt.build.group_overlap. `grep -n 'group_overlap\|horizon_changed' src/opt/api.py docs/04_CONTRACT.md src/spine/compose.py` returns only src/opt/api.py code lines 572, 593, 1151 and 1274. Driving both groups over one shared tensor gives opt.build.group_overlap = 1.

findings.detail: lr_at IS DOCUMENTED PURE AND DOCUMENTED AS PROBEABLE, AND EVERY PROBE PERMANENTLY CORRUPTS FOUR DID IT FIRE COUNTERS. The docstring opens 'PURE: no closure reads, no globals, no measurement' and its P4 note invites the use directly: 'a probe at an arbitrary step gets that step's answer rather than the last one taken.' The body then does `st.counters['opt.lr.in_warmup'] += 1` and the same for damped_this_step, shift_warm_applied and envelope_applied, under a comment that acknowledges the writes but not their reachability from outside. Because lr_at is one of the seven PUBLIC entry points, those four counters measure CALLS-in-state, not steps-in-state, and any caller other than maybe_step silently inflates them. The production loop is safe today and I checked why rather than assuming: spine/compose.py's LOOP_ORDER B row records that lr_at 'is read from inside this one function, which is why it has no row of its own', and docs/04_CONTRACT.md line 3305 repeats it -- so lr_at has no independent call site in the root. That makes this a low-severity trap rather than a live wrong number, but it is a trap laid by the docstring for the exact tool (a probe over a step grid) that the supervisor's own three spot checks used.

Counters after: opt.lr.in_warmup=50, envelope_applied=0, damped_this_step=0, shift_warm_applied=0, opt.step=0. A ledger reporting 50 warmup steps on a run that took zero steps.

findings.detail: THE PARAM-GROUP CLAUSE HOLDS IN FULL, INCLUDING THE GOAL-B HAZARD docs/04_CONTRACT.md WARNS ABOUT, AND I PROVED IT WITH A GRADIENT STEP RATHER THAN A COUNT. spine/compose.py hands build() `param_groups={'base': sysm.base_params, 'encoder': list(sig_api.encoder_parameters(sig, sysm.sig))}` where sysm.base_params = spine/compose.py::_base_parameters, which concatenates LM.model, FAB.population and WORLD.world's parameters() and appends a System.warnings line for any object exposing none. build() then does `ordered = (('base', list(groups.get('base', ()))), ('encoder', list(groups.get('encoder', ()))))` and constructs one AdamW per group over an explicit param-group dict. Nothing handed in is dropped: with three base tensors of shapes (3), (2,2) and (5) plus one encoder tensor, param_group_shape is (('base', 3, ((3,), (2,2), (5,))), ('encoder', 1, ((4,),))), the id-set of the three tensors handed in equals the id-set inside st.base exactly (no missing, no extras), and after one scaled_backward+maybe_step ALL THREE moved by 3.999e-05 while the encoder tensor moved by 0.0 with its .grad still populated -- which is Q-OPT-6 exactly as declared, the encoder rate written but the step left to SIG. The empty-group reasoning is true as stated and I checked the torch claim rather than trusting it: `torch.optim.AdamW([], lr=1e-3)` raises ValueError('optimizer got an empty parameter list') and `torch.optim.AdamW([{'params': []}], lr=1e-3)` is accepted. So a package contributing nothing yields base=0/encoder=0 counters and a shape row of ('base', 0, ()), never a crash and never a silent absence. A key that is neither 'base' nor 'encoder' is refused by name. Every one of the twelve declared startup refusals fires -- lr_restart_damp >1.0 and <0.0, lr<=0, weight_decay<0, lr_min_frac at 1.0 and -0.1, lr_decay 1.1, lr_warmup -1, lr_wavelength -1, accum 0, batch_windows 0, grad_clip -1 -- each a ValueError carrying the generated env name.
findings.repro: build(cfg, param_groups={'base': [a,b,c], 'encoder': [e]}, run_windows=U.Windows(1000)) with a,b,c,e nn.Parameters of ones; loss = 2*a.sum() + 3*b.sum() + 4*c.sum() + 5*e.sum(); scaled_backward then maybe_step -> StepOutcome(stepped=True, lr=4e-05, ...) and max|delta| per tensor: a 3.999e-05, b 3.999e-05, c 3.999e-05, e 0.000e+00. Group variants: {'base': [], 'encoder': [a]} -> BUILT, base=0 encoder=1; {'base': [a]} (encoder key absent) -> BUILT, base=1 encoder=0; {'base': [], 'encoder': []} -> BUILT, 0/0; {'base': [a], 'fabric': [a]} -> ValueError naming ['fabric'].

findings.detail: THE ROUND TRIP IS CLEAN ON EVERY FIELD INCLUDING THE RESTART/DAMPING STATE AND THE DID IT FIRE COUNTERS -- the recorded defect is dead. I drove a 1000-step run at OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=200, OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.5, OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=0.01, OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=7 with losing Readings, which left restart_amp=0.5 (one damping applied), cycle_best=38.9, cycle_index=8, lr_prev=1e-4, shift_at=400 and 1000 grad_norms. state_dict wrote all thirteen keys including param_group_shape (the Q-OPT-4 addition that arms the L50 guard) and grad_norms and shift_at (the two P4 additions). I then built a SECOND OptState over identically shaped groups, MUTATED every field away from the saved value first (restart_amp=0.123, cycle_best=-1.0, cycle_index=99, lr_prev=0.777, shift_at=12345, grad_norms=[42.0], opt_step=Steps(5), n_backward=Backwards(5)) so a field that failed to travel would be visible, and load_state'd. Every one came back: opt_step 1000, n_backward 1000, lr_prev 1e-4, restart_amp 0.5, cycle_best 38.9, cycle_index 8, shift_at 400, 1000 grad_norms, and the horizon and param_group_shape are the LIVE ones as documented. The single counter that differs is opt.ckpt.loaded (0 -> 1), which is correct. The behavioural check that matters: lr_at at Steps(500) returns 0.0006378570286113816 on both states -- bit-identical -- so the schedule genuinely resumes at the DAMPED amplitude rather than at full peak. The refusals are armed against a value state_dict actually writes: a payload with param_group_shape removed is refused by name, and _normalised_shape compares nested tuples so a JSON-round-tripped list still matches.
